1. Heard on the application for condonation of delay on filing the present case u/s 5 of the Limitation Act.

It is submitted that the appellant appeared on several date of hearing in the above case before Ld.
Trial Court but due to the lockdown in the early months of 2020, the Courts was also closed and on dilution of effect of Covid-19, the Courts was functioning by virtual mode and many times he went to the office of his counsel Sh. Y.K. Gautam and appeared online before appellant.
Thereafter, the appellant fell ill and physically could not appear in the above case before Ld. Trial Court, as such he was proceed ex-parte on 30.01.2020.

Although, the appellant was continuously in contact with his counsel who was requested to appear on his behalf in the above case before Court and his counsel has been assuring him that he would appear as counsel for the appellant on each and every date of hearing till the appellant recovers from his illness and becomes able to appear personally in the above case before Ld. Trial Court, but the said counsel never apprised the appellant regarding the status and proceedings of the case.
The appellant was surprised to know the disposal of the above case on receiving the summons of the execution petition.
It is submitted that his counsel has concealed the status of the proceedings and orders of the above case.
It is further submitted that the appellant has engaged new counsel Sh. A.A. Khan and the counsel for appellant has immediately filed present appeal.
3. This Court has heard the Ld. Counsel for the appellant as well as Ld. Addl. PP for the State.

Ld.
Addl. PP for the State has vehemently opposed the present application on the ground that no cogent explanation is offered for delay in filing the present appeal.

4. It is noted that the impugned interim order was passed by the Ld. Trial Court on 27.04.2022 whereby the appellant (respondent therein) were directed not to commit any act of domestic violence upon the respondent (petitioner therein).
They were also prohibited from committing any violence against the dependents/ relatives or any other person who assists the respondent (petitioner therein).
Additionally, the appellant was directed to pay an amount of Rs.20,000/- to the respondent as compensation towards the incidents of domestic violence committed upon her.
Appellant was directed to pay Rs.7,000/- p.m. as maintenance to the respondent from the date of filing of the DV petition till the date of disposal of the case.
5. It is not in dispute that the time period prescribed for filing the appeal is three moths from the date of decision.
Present appeal was filed on 15.12.2022 i.e. 110 days after the expiry of prescribed period of limitation for filing the appeal.

In the present application as well as in the memorandum of appeal, the appellant has furnished explanation for not appearing in the proceedings before the Ld.
Trial Court in petition CC No. 256/2019 PS Karawal Nagar.
However, no explanation is furnished for delay in filing the present appeal.

6. At this stage, it is pertinent to note that it has been held in the case of G. Ramagorda v. Special Land Acquisition Officer that, "There is no general principle saving the party from all mistakes of its counsel.

entities.text: G. Ramagorda v. Special Land Acquisition Officer
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If there is negligence, deliberate or gross inaction or lack of bona fides on the part of the party or its counsel there is no reason why the opposite side should be exposed to a time- barred appeal.
Each case will have to be considered on the particularities of its own special facts.

However, the expression 'sufficient cause' in section 5 must receive a liberal construction so as to advance substantial justice and generally delays in preferring appeals are required to be condoned in All Residents Of vs Mamta on 17 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149601380/
2

the interest of justice where no gross negligence or deliberate inaction or lack of bona fides is imputable to the party seeking condonation of the delay; G. Ramagorda v. Special Land Acquisition Officer, AIR 1988 SC 897".

entities.text: G. Ramagorda v. Special Land Acquisition Officer, AIR 1988 SC 897
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
7. It has been held in the case of Shakuntala Devi Jain v. Kuntal Kumari that, "Section 5 gives the courts a discretion which in respect of jurisdiction is to be exercised in the way in which judicial power and discretion ought to be exercised upon principles which are well understood; the words 'sufficient cause' receiving a liberal construction so as to advance substantial justice when no negligence nor inaction nor want of bona fides is imputable to the appellant; Shakuntala Devi Jain v.
Kuntal Kumari, AIR 1869 SC 575."
8.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text:
Shakuntala Devi Jain v.
Kuntal Kumari, AIR 1869 SC 575
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the law as stated above and the fact that no cogent explanation is furnished on behalf of appellant as to why there is delay of 110 days in filing the present appeal, this Court is not inclined to condone the delay.
Accordingly, appeal filed on behalf of appellant is hereby dismissed being time barred.
Copy of this judgment be sent to Ld. Trial Court for intimation.
File be consigned to the record room.
